topic: Building a three-tier application; load balancing and autoscaling
title: Scale the results portal for results day
instructions:
## 400 requests a second at 8 a.m.

When exam results are released, traffic to the portal climbs from 20 to **400 requests per second** in 25 minutes and stays there. A single `small` server serves about 50. Build a deployment that absorbs the peak and shrinks afterwards.

## Do this

1. Create a load balancer `web-lb` in `af-west-1`.
2. Create an autoscaling group `web-asg` of `small` instances, **minimum 2, maximum at least 8**, across zones **a and b**, scaling at **60% CPU** or lower, attached to `web-lb`.
3. Create a managed database `results-db` with **Multi-AZ** and encryption on.
4. On **Monitor**, run `results-day`. Read the log: when did it scale out, how many instances did it reach, and how many requests failed while new instances were starting?
5. Press **Check my deployment**. Keep the monthly estimate under $200.
hints: An autoscaling group needs a load balancer to send traffic to its instances: create the LB first and select it in the ASG form.
New instances take two minutes to start, so scaling at 60% CPU leaves time before the group saturates. A higher minimum costs more but protects the first minutes.
The database tier is separate from the web tier; Multi-AZ keeps a standby in another zone.

checks.label: A load balancer with targets in two zones
checks.name: web-lb

checks.label: Autoscaling 2 to 8+ instances across two zones, scaling at 60% CPU
checks.name: web-asg

checks.label: Results day served with at least 98% availability and a peak of 4+ instances

realityNote: Real autoscaling policies also use request count per target and scheduled scaling: you know results day is coming, so you raise the minimum the night before. Pre-warming the database connection pool and caching the results page matter as much as the instance count.
